post.meaning: One who is restrained in hand, in foot and in speech, who delights inwardly, is composed, solitary and content, is called a true mendicant.
post.caption:
Hatthasaṁyato pādasaṁyato, Vācāsaṁyato saṁyatuttamo;
Ajjhattarato samāhito, Eko santusito tamāhu bhikkhuṁ.

जो हाथ, पैर और वाणी में संयमी है, भीतर से प्रसन्न, एकाग्र, अकेला और संतुष्ट है, उसी को सच्चा भिक्षु कहते हैं।

One who is restrained in hand, in foot and in speech, who delights inwardly, is composed, solitary and content, is called a true mendicant.

— Dhammapada, Verse 362

reel.meaning: Bear with one another and, if anyone has a complaint against another, forgive each other; as the Lord has forgiven you, so you also must forgive.
reel.caption:
Forbearing one another, and forgiving one another, if any man have a quarrel against any: even as Christ forgave you, so also do ye.

एक-दूसरे की सह लो, और यदि किसी को किसी पर दोष देने का कारण हो, तो एक-दूसरे को क्षमा करो; जैसे प्रभु ने तुम्हें क्षमा किया, वैसे ही तुम भी करो।

Bear with one another and, if anyone has a complaint against another, forgive each other; as the Lord has forgiven you, so you also must forgive.

— Colossians (KJV), 3:13
